title: Critic v1: rubric, absolute and order-swapped pairwise modes
description: Read AGENTS.md, NEXT.md and docs/plans/2026-10-09-story-harness.md first. Preserve unrelated changes; do not linewrap Markdown; run npm test before committing. Include the pairwise prompt: two unlabelled stories, which would the commissioning reader publish with fewer edits and why, margin clear/slight or tie, reader questions each answers. Add score (absolute, appends a score row) and pair (writes evals/pairs/<pair_id>/A and B with prose and charts only, a gitignored mapping.json, judges in both orders, appends a pair row whose result is a win only when both orders agree) subcommands. title: oil-prices: explain the historical days missing from the live EIA files
description: Read AGENTS.md, NEXT.md and docs/plans/2026-09-25-next-phase.md first. Preserve unrelated changes; do not linewrap Markdown; run npm test before committing. The monitor research (docs/plans/2026-09-25-research/monitor.md) found the live EIA spot-price files missing about 890 Brent and 743 WTI historical days that are present in our 2026-09-05 snapshot; a second download gave the same bytes. Find out which days, whether EIA revised or truncated the series, whether it is a download/format artefact, and what our dataset should do (keep the snapshot values, flag them, or follow the source). This must be understood before oil-prices is monitored. Also note the SheetJS xlsx advisory status for this build's dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Cause identified or bounded with evidence; README records the finding; follow-up bead if data changes are needed.
notes: 2026-10-10 findings (commit e24166f). Cause: EIA dnav publication defect, not a revision. Evidence vs EIA files released 2026-10-07: RBRTEd.xls drops 890 days (1987-12-21..2014-10-14, mostly 1993-2006; 1994 keeps 138/252), RWTCd.xls drops 743 (1986-01-31..2015-02-04; heavy 1999/2003/2011); 174 dates common. Weekday-uniform, not holidays, not carry-forward prices. 0 value changes on retained days; monthly/annual unchanged. EIA API v2 (petroleum/pri/spt, DEMO_KEY) returns all 890/743 at identical values. EIA weekly averages for 471/475 Brent (450/469 WTI) affected weeks equal the mean of the full snapshot daily data, only 12 match the reduced daily. Weekly xls also randomly dropped 3 Brent / 21 WTI weeks. Rows absent from sheet itself (A1:B9106 vs B9971) and from the HTML leaf RBRTED.htm; repeat downloads byte-identical -> not a download/format artefact. Decision (review-after): keep snapshot values; refresh must use API or union+flag. title: Detect silent source revisions: a shared fetch --refresh and manifest-hash diff helper
description:
Nothing in this repo detects that a source has silently revised a snapshot. Evidence from the second discovery rep: the NWS PDFs carry a `Report generated:` date showing old years were regenerated without notice (2007-2015 all in 2016, 2019 in 2021, 2024 in 2026), and the Tesla releases restate figures without reissuing. With no index there is also no change feed, so re-fetching and diffing is the only way to see it.

Proposed: a shared helper (not a per-dataset habit) that runs a dataset's `fetch.ts --refresh` into a scratch directory and diffs content hashes against the committed archive/manifest.json, reporting which sources changed and by how much, without touching archive/. It would suit any `monitored` dataset. Start by reading the two existing fetch.ts implementations (tesla-quarterly-deliveries, us-natural-hazard-statistics) and extracting only what they already share; do not invent a generic scraping framework. Acceptance: one command per dataset that exits non-zero when a source changed, with a fixture-based test for both the changed and unchanged cases. Do not linewrap Markdown.
notes: 2026-09-25: designed in docs/plans/2026-09-25-research/monitor.md section 2; prototype docs/plans/2026-09-25-research/prototypes/source-diff.mjs gave the right answer on all four real manifests. Interface: scripts/source-diff.mjs, exit 0 unchanged / 1 changed / 2 error, plus an offline manifest-vs-manifest mode; fetchers gain DATAPRESSR_ARCHIVE_DIR (one line each) so a refresh writes to scratch; normalise the id field (source_id vs name). Key finding: a raw hash change is not enough to act on (NOAA rewrites a creation-date comment monthly); the workflow (w83.2) decides on data/ changes after rebuild.

title: CLI entry guard exits 0 silently when the script is reached through a symlinked directory (npm test fails on macOS)
description:
Found 2026-09-19 while re-verifying the cloud runs' work: `npm test` on macOS is 107/108. The failing test is `scripts/validate-datapackage.test.mjs:45` ("the CLI reports and exits 1 even when its own path contains a space"). The cloud runs (Linux) reported 108/108, so it only shows where a temp dir or checkout path goes through a symlink.

Cause: the CLI entry guard `process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` compares a realpath'd URL (Node resolves symlinks for import.meta.url) with a URL built from the raw argv path (symlinks preserved). Reached through a symlinked directory the guard is false and the CLI prints nothing and exits 0, on a package with real errors. This is the same silent-exit-0 defect the guard was written to fix, still present for symlinks. On macOS os.tmpdir() (/var/folders/... -> /private/var/...) and /tmp are symlinks, so the test trips it.

Reproduce: copy scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs to /private/tmp/x/'real dir'/v.mjs, symlink /private/tmp/x/linkdir -> that directory, then `node /private/tmp/x/linkdir/v.mjs scripts/fixtures/bad-name`: exit 0 through the symlink, exit 1 via the real path. `scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs` has the identical guard and the identical failure (verified: exit 1 via real path, exit 0 via symlink).

Files: scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs and its two byte-identical copies datasets/climate-and-environment/co2-ppm/scripts/ and datasets/energy-and-commodities/oil-prices/scripts/ (keep all three identical), scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs, and their tests. Likely fix: compare realpathSync(process.argv[1]) to fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), keeping the bare-import guard on process.argv[1]. Add a test that reaches the CLI through an explicitly created symlink so it does not depend on the platform's tmpdir. Do not linewrap Markdown.
notes: 2026-09-19 fixed. Changed: scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs (and its two byte-identical copies in co2-ppm/scripts and oil-prices/scripts, md5 checked), scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs, and tests scripts/validate-datapackage.test.mjs and scripts/check-invisible-characters.test.mjs. Fix: the entry-point guard now compares import.meta.url with pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href inside a try/catch (realpathSync throws for the undefined argv[1] of node -e and for a missing path, both meaning imported-not-run), replacing the raw-argv comparison. TDD: added a symlinked-directory CLI test for each script (explicit symlinkSync, so they do not depend on the platform tmpdir); before the fix 3 tests failed (both new ones and the existing space test, on macOS), after it all pass. Results: npm test 146/146 (needed npm install in datasets/climate-and-environment/us-natural-hazard-statistics first, the documented per-dataset step), npm run check:invisible clean, validator 0 errors and 0 warnings on all six datasets. Manual edge cases all correct: real path with a non-ASCII and spaced directory, symlink to the file, symlink to the directory, relative path, valid package exits 0, bare import does not run the CLI, invisible check via symlinked directory exits 1. Not done here: an independent review agent (change is a few lines per file, verified by the edge cases above).
close_reason: CLI entry guard now compares against realpath(argv[1]); silent exit 0 via symlinked directory fixed in validate-datapackage (3 copies) and check-invisible-characters, with symlink tests; npm test 146/146 on macOS

title: Tesla worked example: autonomous source discovery, scraping and reproducible quarterly data
description:
Read AGENTS.md, NEXT.md, docs/next-session-brief.md and parent datapressr-03u. This is an end-to-end worked example of an agent starting with a data question, finding suitable sources, scraping them and producing a reproducible dataset with little human direction. The original question is Tesla quarterly sales/deliveries by vehicle over time; source reporting may only support grouped models and some periods. Do not promise finer granularity than the evidence.

Files owned: datasets/transport/tesla-quarterly-deliveries/{AGENTS.md,README.md,datapackage.json,.datahubignore,fetch.ts,build.ts,build.test.mjs,archive/,data/}; optional local package.json/package-lock.json only for a necessary parser; docs/examples/tesla-source-discovery.md. This is one dataset, not an entire Tesla portal/catalog. Do not create a new external repo or publication in this task.

1. Source discovery: start from official Tesla investor-relations quarterly releases, shareholder updates and filings; follow links from official indexes. Verify exact current URLs during execution. Use primary-source copies of historical documents when needed. Compare secondary aggregators only to find gaps or corroborate, never silently substitute estimates. Record search queries, candidate URLs, accepted/rejected sources, retrieval date, reporting coverage, reported model groupings, measurement definitions and license/terms evidence. Aim for all verifiable quarters discoverable from the official archive through the latest completed quarter with a released report; pin an explicit cutoff and record earlier missing periods rather than claim completeness. Discovery budget: 60 minutes; a blocked candidate gets at most 15 minutes before trying an alternative. A documented access limit is a result, not permission to guess.

2. Decide and record the source-backed schema before scraping. Proposed long-form output: period_start (date), period_end (date), vehicle_group (string), metric (string: deliveries or the exact verified measure), vehicles (integer), source_id (string). Primary key: period_start, period_end, vehicle_group, metric. Keep production in a separate metric if included; never relabel it deliveries, and do not equate revenue with unit sales. Preserve reported combined groups verbatim or with an explicit stable mapping; do not split a combined group into individual models or sum overlapping total/component rows. Source revisions need an explicit preferred-version rule with both snapshots retained.

3. Read skills/archive/SKILL.md and skills/structure/SKILL.md. Write fetch.ts for bounded, paced retrieval with explicit timeouts, capped retries and a source manifest containing URL, source_id, retrieval timestamp, content hash, local path and reporting period. Reuse snapshots on rerun unless an explicit refresh is requested. Try plain HTTP first; if a browser is necessary, record exactly what required it and preserve the downloaded document for offline parsing. Respect access restrictions; no credentials, paid services or bypasses. Keep source volume well below the small-data ceiling.

4. Archive evidence before parsing. Record license uncertainty honestly; do not invent a redistribution license. If permissions remain unresolved, retain a stub package and the evidence report, record the blocked publication/structured status and continue useful local verification. Follow repository source/license requirements before advancing lifecycle status.

5. Write build.ts to consume only archived inputs and emit data/tesla-quarterly-deliveries.csv plus a source resource if needed, with typed metadata, primary keys, provenance links and data conventions. Use plain Node and one targeted parser only when required. Preserve true missing values and actual zeros distinctly. Report every discovered quarter as parsed or explicitly unavailable/unsupported; assert malformed tables, duplicate/conflicting keys, unexplained gaps and mismatched source totals rather than silently dropping them.

6. Test extraction against archived fixtures spanning at least two reporting layouts/grouping regimes where available. Assert known source numbers, comma-separated integers, missing vs zero, duplicate/revised quarters and grouped-model behavior. Independently spot-check earliest/latest available quarters plus one grouping change and one revision/exception if present. Rebuild twice without network and compare output hashes. Run node scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs datasets/transport/tesla-quarterly-deliveries and npm test from root.

7. Write docs/examples/tesla-source-discovery.md as a concise walkthrough with runnable fetch/build commands, source-selection rationale, coverage/gaps table, evidence-backed sample results and an autonomy log: decisions made unaided, failed approaches, human interventions (including zero), elapsed time and tools used. State what this example teaches beyond archive/structure, and list concrete follow-up suggestions without inventing a generic scraping framework. README covers definitions, coverage, revisions, license limitations and rerun instructions.

Handoff: append changed files, checks/results, commits, source cutoff and remaining limitations to this Bead. No story, enrichment, publication or generalized discover skill is included. If source access or permissions prevent the acceptance criteria, keep this task open with the precise blocker; do not call a partial scrape complete.
acceptance_criteria: A new agent can reproduce the documented Tesla dataset offline from saved raw sources, and can rerun source retrieval explicitly. Every output row is traceable to a primary source; coverage and unsupported model splits are explicit; source license status is honest. At least two source layouts/grouping regimes tested when available (otherwise evidence explains why only one exists); no unreported model splits or silent quarter loss; deterministic hashes, meaningful tests, zero validator warnings before structured status. Walkthrough reports actual autonomy and limitations. Parent closes only after this worked example is verified.

Findings (plain HTTP, curl): ir.tesla.com (home, /press, press-release pages), assets-ir.tesla.com PDFs, ir.tesla.com/_flysystem SEC PDFs and businesswire.com all return 403 to plain HTTP even with a browser UA (bot protection) — no bypass attempted. SEC EDGAR is the viable primary archive: data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001318605.json (+ -submissions-001.json for 2005-2018) lists every 8-K. Production & deliveries releases are the item-2.02 8-Ks filed 1-5 days after quarter end: 2013-04-01 (Q1 2013), then continuous 2015-04-03 (Q1 2015) .. 2026-07-02 (Q2 2026), with oddities to check: two filings 2017-07-03/2017-07-07, 2018-10-01/2018-10-02, and 2019-10-02 bundled with items 1.01/2.03. Q2-Q4 2013 and all of 2014 are not separate P&D 8-Ks (likely in shareholder letters / earnings 8-Ks). notes:
Verified outcome: charts ported from hand-rolled SVG to Observable Plot.

Changed paths:
- site/stories/make-charts.mjs (rewritten, Plot + jsdom, same pattern as planetary-boundaries-make-charts.mjs)
- site/stories/keeling-annual.svg, site/stories/keeling-seasonal.svg (regenerated)

Commit: c7ecdda (main, pushed)

Commands/results:
- node make-charts.mjs run 3x -> byte-identical SVGs each time (md5sum compared)
- npm test (root) -> 47/47 pass
- 350/400 ppm crossing years computed from co2-annual-mlo.csv itself (find first row >= threshold): 1988 and 2015, matching the pre-existing hardcoded values -- confirms they were correct, now they're derived instead of asserted. Cross-checked against co2-monthly-mlo.csv: first *month* >= 350 is 1986-05, >= 400 is 2013-05 -- materially earlier than the annual-mean crossings. This is exactly the monthly-vs-annual ambiguity the acceptance criteria flagged: chart labels now read "annual mean, crossed <year>" rather than a bare year, so they can't be misread against the well-known monthly milestone dates.
- Seasonal high/low: computed from the most recent full calendar year in the plotted window (2025) rather than hardcoded -- May 2025 (430.51 ppm) high, September 2025 (424.37 ppm) low. Cross-checked against the multi-year average seasonal residual (raw - deseasonalized) across the full monthly record: May has the highest average residual (+3.09), September/October the lowest (-3.24/-3.25) -- confirms May/Sep-Oct is the genuine seasonal pattern, not a one-year fluke.
- Label clipping: no headless browser/screenshot tool is available in this environment, so "screenshots inspected" could not be done literally. Instead verified structurally: (a) both annotation labels use text-anchor="end" anchored at or left of their point with a negative dx, so they grow leftward into the ~650px inner plot width regardless of label length -- estimated left extents (~460-472px) computed from the raw SVG and confirmed clear of the left margin (52px); (b) Plot's generated <style> block sets max-width:100%; height:auto on the <svg>, which is the standard responsive-SVG pattern -- confirmed present in both output files, satisfying the narrow-width requirement structurally.
- Light/dark: NOT independently verified (no browser). Both charts render on a transparent background using fixed dark text/line colours (#111827, #2563eb, etc.) -- this is unchanged from the *existing* planetary-boundaries-make-charts.mjs pattern (also transparent, also fixed colours), so this task introduces no regression, but the underlying risk (illegible dark text on a dark page background, if one is ever rendered) is pre-existing and repo-wide, not specific to Keeling. Flagging rather than unilaterally adding a background rect to only these two charts, since a background/theme convention affects every story chart and reads as a shared/coordinator-level decision, not a file-scoped fix.

Decisions:
- Kept the "annual mean" qualifier as the disambiguation mechanism (in the chart label itself) rather than editing keeling-curve.md prose, since the prose's existing wording ("around 1988", "in 2015") already reads as annual and needed no change, and prose edits were out of this task's file scope.
- Did not add a background rect / address dark-mode legibility -- filed as an open question below rather than a unilateral change.

Open question for the coordinator (not resolved here): should story chart SVGs paint an explicit background (e.g. white) for legibility if ever rendered on a dark page background? Affects planetary-boundaries and Keeling charts alike -- a shared-convention question, not specific to this task.
close_reason: Ported to Observable Plot (c7ecdda): crossing years and seasonal extrema computed from data rather than hardcoded, monthly-vs-annual crossing ambiguity resolved via explicit labelling, byte-identical across reruns, npm test 47/47. title: evals harness: leak-scan false positives, usage-limit handling, critic-skip message
description: From the structure eval round 1 (datapressr-8no.3). (1) Every Claude structure run was flagged leaked; on review all hits were false positives: relative paths like ../../../AGENTS.md from a Bash cwd inside datasets/... (still inside the workspace), and a Read of the CLI's own persisted large-output file under ~/.claude/projects/<workspace-slug>/.../tool-results/, which the deny rule refused. Track cd in the scan or resolve relative paths against the workspace dataset dirs, and treat a denied Read as blocked rather than leaked. (2) Isolation note: claude -p writes per-run ~/.claude/projects/-private-var-...-evals-ws-*/ directories (tool-results) in the user's real ~/.claude despite --no-session-persistence; consider CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per run if auth allows. (3) Three Claude runs in parallel hit the subscription 5-hour limit (result api_error usage_limit_reached); the runner flagged them failed but kept starting repeats. Stop the remaining repeats on usage_limit_reached and give it a distinct flag (or exclude it from per-case tables). (4) run prints 'not scored (--no-critic)' when the critic was skipped because the domain has no rubric.
notes: 2026-10-10 (hcn.11): q01 runs 20261010-1004 and -1012 flagged leaked; reviewed, all false positives. Relative ../ paths resolve inside the workspace; and a new kind: the awk match operator in `awk -F, '$4 ~ /Q4/'` is read by PATH_RE as a bare ~ and reported as /Users/rgrp. The scanner should not treat a lone ~ followed by whitespace as a home path (or should only flag ~ at a command-argument position).

title: Owner decisions: four small repo-convention choices raised by cloud runs
description:
Four small convention choices surfaced by the cloud runs of 2026-09-18/19, each a real trade-off rather than a defect. Decide each and record it here; the agent-ready follow-up is trivial once decided.

1. AGENTS.md "Missing values": add the converse clause? Proposed wording, one clause on the existing bullet: "...Don't mix NA, N/A, -, 0, and empty string for 'missing' within one column, and note the converse: where a literal NA is a real code (North America, Namibia), keep it verbatim and say so in the field description." The skills/structure "Values that lie" block (datapressr-eec) already says this; AGENTS.md was left untouched because the Bead made it conditional on the owner.
2. Worked-example paths in skills/: the four in-repo ones (co2-ppm, oil-prices, population-growth, airports) are repo-relative, so they are clickable in the repo and dead for anyone who installed the skill with `npx skills add datasets/datapressr`. Make them absolute (works everywhere) or keep relative (clickable here)?
3. Per-dataset AGENTS.md copies: currently byte-identical to the root file, which carries repo-level task-tracking (Beads) instructions a dataset that becomes its own repo does not need. Keep byte-identical, or make the copies a dataset-relevant subset? The two rules pull opposite ways.
4. changelog/2026-09-18-tesla-quarterly-deliveries.md covers the Tesla dataset and two structure-skill sections together. Split the skill guidance into its own entry?
notes:
2026-09-19 (from the second cloud run): fifth choice. The adversarial-review step, where a fresh reviewer independently re-derives the numbers and tries to break the build, is a convention of the cloud runs, not a rule in any document. In both source-discovery reps the single most valuable finding came from it (rep 1's wrong coverage rows; rep 2's two latent silent-failure paths). docs/source-discovery-playbook.md says so in its limitations, but neither it nor skills/structure/SKILL.md requires it. Decide whether to require it (and for which lifecycle stage) before discovery is graduated into anything.
2026-09-25 (agent, under the owner's delegation to decide reversible choices and flag for review): (1) Missing-values converse clause ADDED to AGENTS.md. (3) Per-dataset AGENTS.md copies: all six had drifted again, so copies are now the dataset-conventions subset (everything above a repo-only marker in the root file), written by scripts/sync-dataset-agents.mjs and enforced by npm test. (2) Worked-example paths: decided ABSOLUTE GitHub URLs so installed skills work; execution filed in the adoption epic. (4) Do not split the 2026-09-18 Tesla changelog entry: historical, low value. (5) Adversarial review: require it at 'structured' for any dataset with a custom parser or many source documents, recommended otherwise; codification filed in the quality epic. Commit: a86e8d6. Owner review requested after the fact.

title: structure: value semantics — text placeholders, literal NA as data, aggregate flags, source precision
description: Read AGENTS.md and docs/next-session-brief.md first. Claim before editing. Do not linewrap Markdown. Work only in the listed files; record scope expansion as a separate Bead. Handoff: changed paths, commits, commands/results. Files: skills/structure/SKILL.md (extend the sentinel bullet under 'Government / scientific text data' or a new short 'Values that lie' list); optionally AGENTS.md 'Data conventions' one line on literal NA if the owner agrees. Finding: docs/structure-benchmark.md round 2 gap 3; evidence docs/benchmarks/round-2-json.md (region/income 'NA'/'Aggregates' placeholders, trailing spaces, 48 aggregates among 265 entities, decimal:1 display hint) and docs/benchmarks/round-2-join.md (continent NA = North America, iso_country NA = Namibia — read as missing by pandas/R defaults). Reproduce: the skill covers numeric sentinels only. Content: text placeholders -> empty; trim whitespace; legitimate values that tools read as missing stay verbatim with a warning in the field description; statistical portals mixing aggregates and units -> is_aggregate flag, not silent drop/keep; keep source precision, treat display hints as metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Guidance present with both round-2 examples cited; no contradiction with AGENTS.md missing-value rule (empty cell); npm test passes.
notes: Commit 148ef01. Changed: skills/structure/SKILL.md only. New 'Values that lie' block covering text placeholders (decided per row by what it is, per column never global; cleanNumber MISSING_TOKENS named as the trap), central whitespace trim, legitimate values tools read as missing (NA = North America / Namibia) kept verbatim with a field-description warning, is_aggregate flag for aggregates mixed with units, keep source precision and treat display hints as metadata; the 'mixing missing-value conventions' bullet under Common mistakes was qualified so it does not forbid the literal-NA case. title: Extend the invisible-character check to .json and .yaml with a rule that spares archive/ and data/
description:
scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs (commits 4106152, fbd5cdf) checks nine source extensions (.ts .mts .cts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .jsx .py) and never anything under archive/. `.json` and `.yaml` are named gaps in its header. A stray U+00A0 pasted into a hand-written datapackage.json field description would not be caught, nor would one in a CI `run:` block if the repo grows workflow files. No tracked JSON carries one today.

Closing the gap needs a rule first: separate hand-written metadata (datapackage.json, package.json, config) from `archive/` and `data/` payloads, which are records of what a source said and must never be rewritten (airports publishes U+00A0 and U+200B in place names on purpose). Write that rule, extend the scan, add a negative-control test that fails without the extension, keep the existing 25+ tests green. Do not linewrap Markdown.
